drivers: one small team and one release cadence
strong consistency between a post's status, its moderation decision and who may read it
modest scale: one forum, no independent scaling need
no existing systems that must stay separate

alternatives.reason: network calls and distributed data for three small modules that share one Post table and one transaction (moderation changes visibility)
a 'post published' event could later feed notifications, but nothing kept today is asynchronous
no existing system has to stay separate; both sources are being replaced
no part needs a second style yet

style.reason: The simplest design that meets every driver; module boundaries keep accounts, posts and moderation apart inside one deployable.

stack.frontend: React 18 single-page app built with Vite, served by the backend
stack.hosting: one container (app) plus a managed PostgreSQL; chosen by the user at deployment

reasons.backend: D02: Boardly (the user's own code) is Express-style Node.js and M05 adapts its moderation handlers; B's Python code is rebuilt, not reused
reasons.database: D03: A's schema already uses uuid, timestamptz and check constraints, which PostgreSQL supports natively
reasons.frontend: D04: A already routes screens client-side (client-routes.js); a small React SPA keeps that model with a common, well-documented stack
reasons.sessions: D05: server-side sessions in PostgreSQL (connect-pg-simple) behind an http-only cookie, as decided at compatibility
reasons.passwords: D06: argon2id password hashes; neither source shows how passwords are stored
reasons.hosting: D09: no hosting constraint was given; one container keeps the monolith simple

modules.name: platform
modules.responsibility: configuration from environment variables, database pool and migrations, error format, request validation, the can(user, action, post) authorisation function

modules.name: accounts
modules.responsibility: users, password hashing, sign-in and sign-out, cookie sessions, roles

modules.name: posts
modules.responsibility: creating posts, reading one post and the published list under the single read rule

modules.name: moderation
modules.responsibility: the pending queue and publish or reject decisions, recorded with moderator and time; changes a post's status only through the posts module

modules.name: web
modules.responsibility: the React screens: Login, PostList (with compose form), PostDetail, ModerationQueue

entities.name: User
entities.notes: role in {member, moderator}; email unique (lower-cased); B integer ids kept in legacy_id on import

entities.name: Post
entities.notes: body 1..10000 characters; status in {pending, published, rejected} default pending; author_id null only when imported_from = 'B'

entities.name: ModerationDecision
entities.notes: audit of A's moderation decisions (A only changed the status); decision in {published, rejected}; one per post

auth.session: server-side session, http-only secure SameSite=Lax cookie, 7-day idle expiry; no bearer tokens

api.auth: public for published; session (author or moderator) otherwise

design_system.tokens: colour roles (bg, surface, text, muted, accent, danger, success) for light and dark; type scale 14/16/20/28; spacing 4-px base; radius 6

configuration.MAX_POST_LENGTH: fixed at 10000 by decision; not configurable

slices.name: Core loop: sign in, write, moderate, read

decisions.reason: see style: one team, one transaction for status and visibility, modest scale
A is the user's own Express-style code; M05 adapts it; B (Python) is rebuilt
uuid, timestamptz and check constraints from A's schema

decisions.decision: Cookie sessions stored in PostgreSQL; no JWT
REST under /api/v1, errors as {error: {code, message}}, cursor pagination
decisions.reason: one API style; neither source has versioning or an error shape

decisions.decision: Read rule enforced only by platform can(); list and detail use it
All settings from environment variables in platform/config; .env.example with names only
decisions.reason: B hard-coded its signing key; no secrets in code

decisions.decision: No code copied from B; A's moderation handlers adapted
decisions.reason: B is in another language; MIT notice therefore not needed in the app (keep it if any B code is ever copied)
